subject: math
cluster: Work with radicals and integer exponents
intro: An 8-question multiple-choice quiz on operations in scientific notation: converting between forms, multiplying, dividing, adding, subtracting, re-normalizing, and comparing magnitudes in real-world contexts.

items.prompt:
Write $0.000\,062$ in scientific notation.
A) $6.2 \times 10^{-5}$
B) $6.2 \times 10^{-4}$
C) $6.2 \times 10^{5}$
D) $62 \times 10^{-6}$

steps: Move the decimal point to get a coefficient in $[1,10)$: $0.000\,062 \to 6.2$.
Count the places moved: the point moves $5$ places to the right, so the exponent is $-5$.
This gives $6.2 \times 10^{-5}$, so A is correct.
B miscounts the decimal places (only $4$). C uses the wrong sign on the exponent. D has a coefficient $62$ that is not in $[1,10)$, so it is not proper scientific notation.
Multiply the coefficients: $3 \times 2 = 6$.
Add the exponents: $4 + 5 = 9$.
The result is $6 \times 10^{9}$, and $6$ is already in $[1,10)$, so B is correct.
A multiplies the exponents ($4 \times 5 = 20$) instead of adding. C adds the coefficients instead of multiplying. D subtracts the exponents.
Both numbers have the same power of $10$, so add the coefficients: $4.5 + 3.2 = 7.7$.
Keep the shared power of $10$: the exponent stays $6$.
The result is $7.7 \times 10^{6}$, and $7.7$ is in $[1,10)$, so C is correct.

A adds the exponents ($6+6=12$). B multiplies the exponents. D leaves an improperly normalized coefficient (it is the same value but is not the correct form here; the correct coefficient is $7.7$, not $77$).

items.prompt:
Compute $(6 \times 10^{4})(5 \times 10^{3})$ and write the result in proper scientific notation.
A) $30 \times 10^{7}$
B) $3 \times 10^{8}$
C) $3 \times 10^{7}$
D) $30 \times 10^{12}$

steps: Multiply the coefficients: $6 \times 5 = 30$.
Add the exponents: $4 + 3 = 7$, giving $30 \times 10^{7}$.
Re-normalize: $30 = 3 \times 10^{1}$, so $30 \times 10^{7} = 3 \times 10^{8}$, so B is correct.
A stops at $30 \times 10^{7}$ without re-normalizing. C forgets to raise the exponent when rewriting $30$. D multiplies the exponents instead of adding.
Divide the coefficients: $8 \div 4 = 2$.
Subtract the exponents: $7 - 3 = 4$.
The result is $2 \times 10^{4}$, and $2$ is in $[1,10)$, so C is correct.
A adds the exponents ($7+3=10$) instead of subtracting. B multiplies the exponents. D subtracts the coefficients instead of dividing.

items.prompt:
Compute $(7 \times 10^{5}) + (3 \times 10^{4})$ and write the result in proper scientific notation.
A) $1 \times 10^{6}$
B) $10 \times 10^{9}$
C) $7.3 \times 10^{5}$
D) $7.3 \times 10^{9}$

steps: Match the powers of $10$: rewrite $7 \times 10^{5} = 70 \times 10^{4}$.
Re-normalize: $73 \times 10^{4} = 7.3 \times 10^{5}$, so C is correct.
A adds the coefficients without matching powers ($7+3=10$). B and D add the exponents, which is never done when adding numbers.

items.prompt:
A bacterium has length $2 \times 10^{-6}$ m. If $0.0003$ of a meter of these bacteria were lined up end to end, scientists instead ask: what is the total length of $3 \times 10^{4}$ such bacteria laid end to end, in meters?
A) $6 \times 10^{-2}$ m
B) $6 \times 10^{-24}$ m
C) $6 \times 10^{2}$ m
D) $5 \times 10^{-2}$ m

steps: Multiply the number of bacteria by the length of one: $(3 \times 10^{4})(2 \times 10^{-6})$.
Multiply the coefficients: $3 \times 2 = 6$.
Add the exponents: $4 + (-6) = -2$.
The result is $6 \times 10^{-2}$ m, and $6$ is in $[1,10)$, so A is correct.
B multiplies the exponents ($4 \times -6 = -24$). C mishandles the sign of the negative exponent. D adds the coefficients instead of multiplying.

items.prompt:
The Sun's mass is about $2 \times 10^{30}$ kg and Earth's mass is about $6 \times 10^{24}$ kg. About how many times more massive is the Sun than Earth?
A) About $3.3 \times 10^{5}$ times
B) About $3 \times 10^{-6}$ times
C) About $3.3 \times 10^{54}$ times
D) About $3.3 \times 10^{6}$ times

steps: Divide the Sun's mass by Earth's mass: $\dfrac{2 \times 10^{30}}{6 \times 10^{24}}$.
Divide the coefficients: $2 \div 6 = \frac{1}{3} \approx 0.333$.
Subtract the exponents: $30 - 24 = 6$, giving $0.333 \times 10^{6}$.
Re-normalize: $0.333 \times 10^{6} = 3.33 \times 10^{5} \approx 3.3 \times 10^{5}$, so A is correct.
B inverts the comparison (Earth over Sun). C multiplies the exponents instead of subtracting. D forgets to lower the exponent when re-normalizing $0.333$ to $3.33$.
